title: Present Tenses
desc: Learn how to talk about habits, current situations, experiences and ongoing actions.

lessons.title: Present Simple: Meaning and Uses
lessons.desc: Habits, routines, facts, permanent situations and feelings.

b.x: The Present Simple is the most common tense in English. We use it to talk about things that are *generally true* or that happen *regularly*, not about what is happening at this exact moment.
Despite its name, the Present Simple is not only about "now". It describes the present as a general period: your life these days, your habits and the way the world works.
None of these sentences is about one moment right now. The first describes a regular situation, the second a habit, the third asks about a habit, and the fourth states a fact.
We use the Present Simple for the things we do regularly: our daily routine.

x: My sister *goes* to the gym after work.

b.x: Ask yourself: "Do I do this again and again?" If the answer is yes, the Present Simple is usually the right tense.
We also use it for actions that repeat at regular times, even if they are not part of a daily routine. Time expressions such as *every Sunday* or *once a week* often appear in these sentences.
Facts, scientific truths and things that are always true use the Present Simple. They do not depend on a particular time, so we do not need a time expression.

x: Cats *sleep* for many hours a day.

b.x: We use the Present Simple to describe situations that are permanent or last for a long time: where someone lives, where they work, what something is like.

x: My grandparents *live* in a small town by the sea.

b.x: For a *temporary* situation, English usually prefers the Present Continuous: "I'm staying with friends this week." You will study this contrast in a later lesson.
Verbs that describe feelings, opinions and preferences are normally used in the Present Simple, even when we mean "right now".
These verbs describe states, not actions, so we usually do not use them in the Present Continuous. We say "I know", not "I am knowing".
Some words and phrases often go with the Present Simple. They show that something is regular or general.

sections.h: A quick look at the form

b.x: The form has its own lesson. For now, remember these three patterns:
In negative sentences and questions, the main verb has no -s: "She doesn't work", not "She doesn't works".
Both tenses talk about the present, but they show different things. The Present Simple is for what is regular or general. The Present Continuous is for what is happening now or for a short time.
We will compare these two tenses in detail in a later lesson.

x: With he, she and it, add -s or -es to the verb.
I am go to school every day.
I go to school every day.
Do not use am, is or are before the verb in the Present Simple.
Use *doesn't*, not *don't*, with he, she and it.
After *do* or *does*, the verb has no -s.
I'm going to the gym every day.
I go to the gym every day.
For habits and routines, use the Present Simple.
Use the Present Simple for habits, routines and repeated actions.
Use it for facts, general truths and permanent situations.
Use it for feelings, opinions and preferences: *love*, *like*, *think*, *want*.
Time expressions such as *every day*, *on Mondays* and *usually* often go with it.
With he, she and it, add -s or -es to the verb in positive sentences.

practice.title: Choose and complete
practice.intro: Pick the best answer or type the correct form of the verb.

items.q: Choose the correct sentence about a daily routine.
options: I am wake up at 7 every day.
I wake up at 7 every day.
I wakes up at 7 every day.
I waking up at 7 every day.
items.explain: With *I*, use the base form of the verb: *I wake up*. Do not add *am* or -s.

items.q: Which sentence describes a habit?
items.explain: *Every day* shows a regular action, so we use the Present Simple. *Now* goes with the Present Continuous.

items.q: Which sentence states a general truth?
items.explain: A general truth is always true, so we use the Present Simple.

items.q: Your sister has taught at a primary school for years. How do you describe this permanent situation?
options: She teaches at a primary school.
She is teaching at a primary school.
She teach at a primary school.
She teached at a primary school.
items.explain: A long-term job is a permanent situation: Present Simple, with -s after *she*.

items.q: My brother ___ (work) in a bank.
items.explain: *My brother* means *he*, so add -s: *works*.

items.q: Water ___ (freeze) at 0°C.
items.explain: This is a fact, so use the Present Simple. *Water* means *it*, so add -es: *freezes*.

items.q: We ___ (go) to the gym every Tuesday.
items.explain: With *we*, use the base form of the verb: *go*.

items.q: Maria ___ (visit) her parents every Sunday.
items.explain: *Maria* means *she*, so add -s: *visits*.

practice.title: Habit, fact, opinion or situation?
practice.intro: Decide what each sentence describes, then build two sentences and write about your own routine.

items.q: What does this sentence describe? “I wake up at 7 every day.”
items.explain: *Every day* shows a regular routine.

items.q: What does this sentence describe? “The Earth revolves around the Sun.”
items.explain: It is always true, whatever the time.

items.q: What does this sentence describe? “He works for an international company.”
items.explain: It describes his long-term job.

items.q: What does this sentence describe? “I love traveling.”
items.explain: *Love* expresses a feeling or preference.

items.q: What does this sentence describe? “Water freezes at 0°C.”
items.explain: It is a scientific fact.

items.q: What does this sentence describe? “She visits her parents every Sunday.”
items.explain: A regular, repeated action works like a habit.

items.q: Put the words in the correct order.
items.explain: Subject + *doesn't* + base verb: *She doesn't drink coffee*.

items.q: Put the words in the correct order.
items.explain: Present Simple questions start with *Do* or *Does*.

items.q: Write five sentences about your own daily routine. Use the Present Simple.
items.model: I wake up at 7 o'clock. I have breakfast at home. I go to work by bus. I finish work at 5 p.m. In the evening, I watch TV with my family.
items.explain: Check that every verb is in the Present Simple. Add -s only when you write about he, she or it.

items.q: Anna introduces herself at a party: “Hi, I'm Anna. I ___ in a hospital.”
items.explain: Anna says *I*, so use the base form: *work*.

items.q: A: What does your father do? B: He ___ for a software company.
items.explain: *He* needs -s in a positive Present Simple sentence: *works*.

items.q: Which sentence states a fact?
options: The sun rises in the east.
items.explain: Facts about the world use the Present Simple.

items.q: My sister ___ (not / like) spicy food.
items.explain: With *she*, the negative is *doesn't* + base verb.

items.q: ___ you play tennis on Saturdays?
items.explain: Questions with *you* start with *Do*.

items.q: Which sentence expresses a preference?
items.explain: *Love* shows what you like, and verbs of feeling use the Present Simple.

items.q: Which sentence has a mistake?
options: She visits her parents every Sunday.
He work for an international company.
items.explain: It should be *He works*. With he, she and it, add -s.

items.q: Put the words in the correct order.
items.answer: My parents live in a small town.
items.explain: Subject + verb + place. *Parents* means *they*, so no -s: *live*.
